title: Chain Mail Periodic Table
one_liner: Explore qudit-pair link types mapped to forces, and evaluate the spoken alpha formula against the measured value.
speaker: Alex Wissner-Gross
context: Alex described chain theory: the world is made of maximally entangled pairs of finite quantum systems. Each pair of dimensions maps to a force (2-2 spacetime, 3-2 electromagnetism, 3-3 strong, 4-2 weak, 4-3 Yukawa, 4-4 Higgs). Pairs with a dimension product of eight or more allow undistillable 'dark' states.
demo: Visitors see a grid of qudit dimensions 2–6 on each axis. Clicking a cell shows the force Alex assigned to it, or 'unassigned/speculative'. Cells with a product of 8 or more get a 'bound-entanglement possible' shading as dark-sector candidates. A side panel evaluates the spoken formula (79 + 48√2 + 42√3 + 3√6)/(24·36²) step by step and shows its inverse next to the quoted 137.035999… value with the digit-by-digit match highlighted.
data_plan: A bundled table of the mappings and formula as stated on the podcast. All arithmetic is computed in-browser. Clearly labelled as one researcher's new, unreviewed theory.
risks: The theory isn't peer-reviewed. Evaluating the formula exactly as transcribed gives about 0.0073006 (inverse about 137.0), not a 10-digit match with 1/137.035999. The transcript may have garbled it, so the page must show the computed mismatch honestly rather than claim agreement. Mappings above 4-4 are not from the episode.
